newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN SAY TABAREZ SAFE DESPITE CUP DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN SAY TABAREZ SAFE DESPITE CUP DEFEAT.

text.p: AC Milan, knocked out of the Italian Cup by Vicenza on Wednesday, insisted on Thursday that Uruguayan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez would have their continued support for the rest of the season.
"Stop this knocking articles about Tabarez," club vice-president Adriano Galliani told reporters at Milan's training ground when asked about his future.
"Whatever results Milan gets in the next matches, Tabarez will stay the Milan coach.
"He will be until June 30, 1997. Then at the end of the season, after looking at the results, we will decide."

Galliani said however that the club had hoped to do well in the cup, although it was only the third priority after the European Cup and league title, and Milan's billionaire owner Silvio Berlusconi was "disappointed" by the defeat.
Vicenza won through to the last four on an away goal after the second leg of their quarter-final ended 0-0.

Striker George Weah, suspended from Milan's home European Cup match against Norway's Rosenborg on Wednesday after a head-butting incident, said the club had the players to do well but four or five of them were not playing as a team.
"It's not the coach's fault if we are not winning," the Liberian said. "Milan has great players but...we have to learn to play together, to help and fight together."
"I need the team to play. I need the ball. I am a striker. I can't always pick up the ball half way down the pitch and score on my own. Maybe two or three times but not always."
Champions Milan are currently a disappointing eighth in serie A, five points behind league leaders Vicenza.
Tabarez took over as coach from the start of the season after his highly-successful predecessor Fabio Capello left for Real Madrid. Real are top of the Spanish league.
